backbone: Equation s(k+h)x+b=c in one real variable, with k a constant parameter, b≠c, nonzero h and b, and either s=1 (direct) or |s|=2..9 (scaled). Ask for k so the equation has no solution; the response is its scalar value in a singleton math blank. Subtract b from both sides, identify a=s(k+h) and the nonzero c-b, set a=0, divide the outer scale when present, then isolate k=-h.

variable.dependent: all variable references in prompt and every solution stage

parameter.dependent: all parameter prose, answer prefix, coefficient equations and final solution

scale.allowed: easy 1; moderate -7,-2,2,3; hard -9,-7,-2; complete source tuples retained
scale.variety: A changed outer scale may change the normalized supplied constants and coefficient division arithmetic; uniform entire-equation scaling is deduplicated.

left.role: constant to remove from left side
left.allowed: finite constant-pair catalog, including nonzero extrema and complete source tuples
left.dependent: equation, inverse operation and right difference

right.allowed: finite constant-pair catalog, including zero, signed extrema, and complete source tuples
right.dependent: equation and subtraction stage; c-b must be nonzero

ordered_solution: state ax=b criterion with b nonzero
subtract left constant on both sides
scaled only: divide nonzero outer scale

sources.full_prompt:
Consider the equation in the variable $x,$ given by

$$
2(p-4)x+2=5
$$

where $p$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $p?$

$p=$
{{field-1}}
sources.full_worked_solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, let's write our equation in the form $ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(p-4)x+2 & =5 \\ 2(p-4)x+2-2 & =5-2 \\ {{2(p-4)}_{⏟}}_{a}x & ={{3}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
2(p-4)=0.
$$

Solving this for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(p-4) & =0 \\ \frac{2(p-4)}{2} & =\frac{0}{2} \\ p-4 & =0 \\ p & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
